themes_detail.label: Homeless Encampments Surge
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints in CD313 spiked to 7 reports THIS WEEK, a 700% increase versus the 0.9 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.61), signaling a potential clustering or visibility crisis in Coney Island/Brighton Beach that warrants street-level investigation.
evidence: 7 encampment complaints filed THIS WEEK (w/o 12/16–12/22 or comparable current week)
0.9 complaints per week baseline over prior 8 weeks = 778% spike
Z-score 6.61 indicates statistically exceptional deviation; 'high severity' flag
reporting_angles: Field reporting: locate visible encampments along Coney Island boardwalk, under overpasses, or in parks; interview residents and outreach workers on causes and duration
City services gap: cross-reference with DSNY, NYPD, and outreach team logs to determine why complaints accelerated this week and what services are deployed

themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Complaints Double
themes_detail.summary: Indoor Air Quality complaints hit 8 reports last week, a 300% spike versus the 2.0 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 5.37), suggesting possible heating failures, mold outbreaks, or ventilation breakdowns across residential or commercial buildings in the district.
evidence: 8 indoor air quality complaints filed last week vs. 2.0 weekly average = 300% increase
Timing coincides with winter heating season; potential HEAT/HOT WATER connection (1,018 complaints over 90 days is high-volume baseline)
reporting_angles: Health angle: contact NYC Department of Health to identify whether there are confirmed mold, CO, or respiratory outbreaks tied to these complaints; interview affected tenants
Housing enforcement: cross-check DOB permits (210 filed in 90 days) and HPD violations to see if recent alterations or deferred maintenance are linked to air quality failures

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement & Public Drinking Spike
themes_detail.summary: Both Vendor Enforcement and Drinking complaints each jumped to 4 reports 2 weeks ago (or last week for Drinking), representing a 3100% spike versus 0.1 weekly averages (z-scores: 11.72 both), pointing to potential informal economy or substance-use clustering near boardwalk, beaches, or commercial corridors.
evidence: Vendor Enforcement: 4 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly avg = 3100% spike (z-score 11.72)
Drinking: 4 complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly avg = 3100% spike (z-score 11.72)
Both flagged 'high severity'; suggests possible geographic or temporal cluster (season-end tourist activity, holiday foot traffic, or enforcement sweep)
reporting_angles: Economic activity: interview street vendors, community board members, and NYPD enforcement to understand whether complaints reflect informal vendors seeking income or unlicensed commercial activity
Public health & safety: investigate whether drinking complaints cluster near specific venues (bars, parks, beaches) and whether NYPD or Parks Enforcement is responding

themes_detail.label: Street Sign Damage & Missing Infrastructure
themes_detail.summary: Damaged street signs spiked to 5 complaints last week (700% vs. 0.6 weekly avg, z-score 6.29) and missing signs hit 4 complaints 3 weeks ago (700% vs. 0.5 avg, z-score 4.95), suggesting rapid deterioration of traffic/directional signage that could indicate storm damage, vandalism, or deferred maintenance in the district.
evidence: Damaged street signs: 5 complaints last week vs. 0.6 avg = 700% spike (z-score 6.29)
Missing street signs: 4 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.5 avg = 700% spike (z-score 4.95)
Combined signal suggests systematic or event-driven infrastructure failure; may correlate with recent weather (snow/ice complaints at 483 over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Infrastructure audit: FOIL NYC DOT work orders for CD313 to determine whether signs were removed for repair, storm-damaged, or neglected; cross-check 'Street Condition' complaints (268 over 90 days)
Community impact: map damaged/missing sign locations and interview residents/merchants on navigation hazards or safety concerns

themes_detail.label: Missed Trash Collection Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Missed Collection complaints spiked to 7 reports 2 weeks ago, a 600% jump versus 1.0 weekly average (z-score: 4.54), indicating possible sanitation service gaps or route failures that may be leaving waste accumulating in neighborhoods.
evidence: Missed Collection: 7 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.0 weekly avg = 600% spike (z-score 4.54)
Flagged 'high severity'; no recent follow-up data showing recovery to baseline
Contextual concern: 'Unsanitary Condition' complaints at 241 over 90 days; possible cascading issue if collection failures are leaving waste on streets
reporting_angles: Service failure: contact DSNY to determine whether there were crew absences, vehicle breakdowns, or route changes 2 weeks ago affecting CD313
Resident impact: visit streets with multiple missed-collection complaints to document conditions and interview residents on health/pest effects
